title: RoboTenon modular architecture and parallel execution (2026-09-20)
p: RoboTenon uses common interfaces for tasks, workflow graphs, capability calls, environment feedback, and action execution in simulation and on physical robots. Plugins and resource settings describe deployment-specific behavior. Single tasks and batches share a lifecycle. Each deployment must verify training and inference consistency and the reliability of its hardware.

tr.td: TaskAdapter
Enumerate TaskCase instances and run an individual case
Experiment setup and task execution
GraphRuntime and Module
Schedule nodes and produce decisions and ActionChunks
Task
ToolRuntime
Provide models, memory, skills, and clients
Worker, with session caches cleared after a task
Environment
Manage sessions, reset, observe, command, and feedback
Task. An external service can remain available independently.
Body
Admit and execute actions, acknowledge completion, and stop the device
Task. An external service can remain available independently.
Monitor
Observe periodically or on demand and publish safety findings
Task or external service

whiteboard: flowchart LR A[TaskAdapter enumerates tasks] --> C[Parent schedules and aggregates] C --> W[WorkerRuntime] W --> T[Resident ToolRuntime] W --> G[Per-task GraphRuntime and Module] G -->|Capability call| T G -->|ActionChunk| B[Body] B -->|Execute and stop| D[Simulator or device driver] G -->|Reset and observe| E[Environment] E -->|Feedback| G E --> M[Monitor] M --> S[Shared safety state] S --> B S --> G
p: runtime.execution.backend selects a registered execution backend. Built-in options are in_process and process. plugin_backends and backend_params support external implementations with declared capabilities. The process backend spawns persistent Workers. Each Worker runs one task at a time with explicit GPU, EGL, and exclusive-resource assignments. Tools can reuse weights and connections. Each task receives fresh Environment, Body, Module, and context objects. Operators deploy external model services independently and assign their devices explicitly.

The parent process schedules work and owns global state. Workers return results and write per-attempt artifacts. Concurrent tasks can finish out of order. Final aggregation follows case order. Batch memory defaults to snapshot mode: tasks read the same input snapshot and their results are merged. Use sequential mode with one Worker when later tasks need to see earlier writes.

The physical-robot template uses one Worker, zero automatic retries, and an exclusive robot resource. Resource locks cover processes belonging to one user on one host. Deployments must implement and verify device drivers, hardware emergency stops, and device-level exclusion.
whiteboard: flowchart LR A[Task or Workers] -->|Execution IDs and events| I[Configured writer] I --> Q[Trace SQLite and JSONL] I --> R[Metrics JSONL] Q -->|Read-only source| W[Web interface] R --> W O[Frame index and media directory] --> W
p: Parallel runs can configure a shared writer, while individual tasks can use their own store. The web interface reads explicit data sources. It does not infer launch mode, discover databases, or replay logs. Trace SQL does not contain all metrics and media. Configure experiment metadata, trace identity filters, and the image index separately.

Records carry experiment, run, episode, attempt, task, adapter, worker, and gpu identities. A run-managed web instance provides read-only observation and shuts down when the run ends. An independently launched web instance with ExperimentManager supports experiment browsing, submission, and configuration management.

tr.td: Graph node or safety event
The Graph and safety configuration determine handling. An explicit ContextStore can retain state and the execution cursor.
Worker loss or process task timeout
While the parent is alive, max_retries controls process recreation and new attempts.
Ordinary task failure
Record the outcome. Worker-loss retries do not apply.
Coordinator crash
Automatic recovery and batch scheduling takeover were unavailable at the report date.
Observability write error
Bounded buffering and failure counters are available. Crashes can lose or duplicate records.

p: After a physical action completes, a crash can occur before its acknowledgement is durable. Recovery requires device-side idempotency and state reconciliation. Body's software stop complements the hardware safety system.

On 2026-09-18, the full suites under local Python 3.11 and server Python 3.12 each reported 179 passing tests. Coverage included process execution, injected faults, lifecycle isolation, and observability reads and writes. At that date, physical GPU/EGL load tests and real-device safety acceptance were still outstanding.
Potential future work includes persistent coordinator takeover, reliable telemetry delivery, and media index aggregation.

See docs/README.md and docs/quickstart.md for entry points, or docs/execution-and-observability.md for configuration, commands, artifacts, and recovery. Historical audits and verification records carry their own dates. This report is an XML fragment with multiple top-level elements intended for document import.

In addition to the six application plugin types, execution backends, four storage types, and streaming RPC transports have independent registration points. Environment RPC handles calls such as reset, observe, and health across processes. Body owns action execution. Custom observation modalities can pass through ObservationFrame, the cache, and ObservationRef. Plugin parameters merge recursively across configuration, TaskCase, and requests. Resource cleanup runs after failed startup as well as ordinary shutdown. See docs/infrastructure-plugins.md for configuration, compatibility aliases, and verification coverage.
